summary.text: 教 means “teach” or “instruct.” Early analyses connect 攴 with a teaching-related action and identify 爻 as a sound element. Accounts differ over whether 子 was present in the earliest form and how the present left side developed.

formation.text: A plausible early formation is phonosemantic: 攴 contributes a teaching-related action, while 爻 is identified as the sound element. Old Chinese comparisons are compatible with that proposed relation, though their initials differ. Some analyses include 子 as a semantic element representing a learner; another account says it was added later. A modern proposal reads the right-hand element in some early forms as 父. The transmitted Shuowen account analyzes 敎 as 攴 plus 𡥉 and interprets teaching through the example set above and imitation below; this is a historical analysis, not independent proof of the graph’s original construction.

components.text: In analyses of 教, 攴 contributes a teaching-related action. One interpretation proposes that it depicts a teaching implement in the scene, but that object identification is not established. 攵 is the conventional side form of 攴, not a separate historical replacement.

The present graph contains 孝. One disputed account proposes that it developed graphically from 𡥉, analyzed there as 爻 plus 子; other accounts reject or differ on this connection. The proposed ancestry is unsettled, and checked sound evidence does not support 孝 as the early sound element.

sound.text: These current readings differ and do not establish an ancient sound role for 孝.

components.text: The CUHK analysis identifies 爻 as the phonetic element in early forms of 教. Baxter–Sagart forms share a final sequence but differ in prefixes; Zhengzhang forms have comparable rhyme sequences but different initials. These comparisons are compatible with the proposed relationship, not independently conclusive. The referent of 爻’s marks and any original spoken name remain unresolved.

sound.text: The current readings provide a modern comparison but do not establish the ancient sound relation.
These Baxter–Sagart forms share a final sequence but differ in prefixes, so they are compatible with the proposed relationship rather than an exact match.

This is the alternate 教 reading for “teaching; instruction,” compared with the same 爻 element; the Baxter–Sagart forms share a rhyme sequence but differ in prefixes and suffix.

components.text: Some analyses of early 教 include 子 as a semantic element representing the learner; another account says it was added later, so its presence in the earliest structure is disputed.

history.text: Accounts differ on the early graphic structure. Some describe 攴, 子, and 爻 together; another says 攴 and 爻 came first and 子 was added later. A modern proposal reads the right-hand element as 父 in some forms. The sequence of graphic changes remains unsettled.

Some accounts report forms with 攴 plus 學 in bronze inscriptions and 言 in Warring States manuscripts. Whether forms with 學 reflect interchange between 教 and 學 is disputed: one report records the forms, while another argues that 教 and 學 began as distinct graphs and were later interchanged.
The transmitted form 敎 is analyzed as 攴 plus 𡥉. Its accompanying explanation connects teaching with enactment above and imitation below.

uncertainties.text: The earliest component structure and graphic changes leading to the present left side remain disputed. The evidence does not settle whether 孝 descends from 爻 plus 子, whether 子 was present from the start, or the direction and date of any change.
爻 is the best-supported sound element in analyses of early forms. The checked Baxter–Sagart readings distinguish 教 from 孝; the referent of 爻’s marks and any original spoken name remain unresolved.

senses.period: Bronze and Warring States manuscript uses reported; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Teaching and instruction are reported in bronze and Warring States manuscript contexts. Oracle-bone occurrences are also interpreted as “instruct,” alongside reported personal or place-name uses and readings such as transmit, cause, or command. These uses and interpretations do not establish a semantic sequence or the graph’s original meaning.
An oracle-bone context is interpreted as command or cause. Its relation to the teaching sense is unresolved.

senses.period: Bronze and Warring States manuscript uses reported; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Bronze and manuscript contexts are reported with 教 meaning teaching or instruction. They do not establish a fully dated path from reported oracle-bone uses.
A historical dictionary records the sense “school,” but no dated example establishes when it arose.
A dictionary records “admonition”; its chronology and relation to teaching are unresolved.
Doctrine and religious teaching are recorded meanings, but their development from the teaching sense is not dated here.
“Class” is listed as a current gloss, but no contextual example or history is supplied.

limitations.text: The accounts do not establish a complete dated sequence, a transition from reported name uses to teaching, or the development of school, admonition, doctrine, and class senses. These meanings are therefore left unconnected.

items.caption: A modern digital rendering of 教 in seal-script style, representing a later form recorded in the Shuowen tradition.
items.alt: Black seal-style character 教 with a crossed, angular form on the left and a tall curving form on the right.
items.selection_reason: The image clearly shows 教 and offers a useful visual reference for the later seal-style form. It does not establish the disputed structure of the earliest forms.
